This land is not mine — I rent it, so I will not spend too much cash on it. I planted yam and cassava last season and got a fair harvest; I will do the same this year. I will put a small bag of NPK on the yam mounds because my neighbor did it last year and his tubers came out bigger, and I will carry goat droppings from my compound to spread on the mounds too. For seed I use my own yam setts from last harvest and cassava cuttings from my brother's farm — improved cuttings are hard to find here and cost money I do not have.

I will not irrigate — the rains here are enough for yam and cassava. I will spray a little herbicide at the start to save my back from too much weeding, but no other chemicals. My wife and my two older children help me, and at mound-making time I will hire a few young men from the village for about a week because making yam heaps alone on nearly one hectare is too much work.
